full_judgment: 27. This very provision of section 152 of the Ordinance came up for consideration before a Single Bench of this court and the case has been reported in 46 DLR 295 wherein it has been held that notice under section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 is a prerequisite in all circumstance for institution of a suit against Pourashava for anything done in official capacity. That suit was instituted for permanent injunction restraining the Narayangonj Pourashava from interfering with the plaintiff's possession in the suit land. The case of the plaintiff was that he was the owner of the property recorded in his name in RS khatian which orginally appertained to CS plot No.278 and the contention of Pourashava was that the suit land was part of CS plot No.279 appertaining to khatian No.670 belonging to the Pourashava and the plaintiff who got his name mutated in the Pourashava papers by fraudulent means was an unauthorised occupant therein and, as such, liable to be evicted. Non-maintainability of the suit for want of notice under section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance was also pleaded in the defence.
